stories.title: AIIMS Delhi performs first fetal surgery for spinal defect
stories.summary: A team at AIIMS Delhi performed India's first prenatal surgery on November 12, repairing a severe spinal defect in a 25-week-old fetus. The six-hour multidisciplinary procedure involved over 30 professionals and required surgeons to lift the baby's back through a uterine incision. Both patients are reportedly stable.

stories.title: AIIMS Delhi Performs India’s First Fetal Surgery to Repair Unborn Baby’s Spine - The Indian Practitioner
stories.summary: Doctors at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi, have achieved a major milestone in fetal medicine by successfully performing India’s first prenatal surgery to repair a severe spinal defect in an unborn baby. The six-hour procedure was performed on November 12 at 25 weeks of pregnancy at

AIIMS Delhi performs six-hour fetal surgery to treat rare spinal condition
stories.summary: The six-hour surgery was performed on an unborn baby at 25 weeks of gestation to repair a severe spinal defect. The multidisciplinary procedure involved more than 30 doctors and healthcare professionals and was provided free of cost to the family. AIIMS Delhi has performed India's first open foetal surgery to

stories.title: Injectable hydrogel shows potential for tissue regeneration
stories.summary: A University of Houston biomedical engineer has developed an injectable peptide hydrogel designed to stimulate blood vessel growth and support healing tissue. The material, which has the consistency of hand sanitizer, offers a customizable blueprint for regenerative medicine, according to findings published in Science Advances.

stories.title: Shared molecular trait identified in glioblastoma cells
stories.summary: Researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai have identified a shared molecular trait in glioblastoma cells that resembles those used during early brain development. This characteristic may provide a target for future treatments of the aggressive adult brain cancer.

stories.title: Targeting immune overactivity in Down syndrome shows promise in phase 2 clinical trial - Medical Xpress
JAK inhibitor trial shows promise for Down syndrome
stories.summary: A phase 2 clinical trial found that the medication tofacitinib reduced immune overactivity and improved inflammatory skin conditions in adolescents and adults with Down syndrome. Published in Cell Reports Medicine, the study also noted preliminary improvements on selected neurobehavioral assessments.

stories.title: MS therapy linked to preserved cognitive function
stories.summary: Pooled results from 280 patients show that those treated with Mavenclad maintained cognitive function over four years. The therapy also reduced relapses and limited disability progression in patients with highly active relapsing multiple sclerosis. Sustained control of inflammatory disease activity was observed in MRI results.

stories.title: Early rituximab use eases myasthenia gravis symptoms
stories.summary: A real-world study indicates that using rituximab within two years of diagnosis eases symptoms and reduces corticosteroid requirements in adults with generalized myasthenia gravis. The benefits were observed in patients with late-disease onset and those with hard-to-treat forms of the condition.

stories.title: Metformin explored as potential Wilson disease treatment
stories.summary: Wilson disease causes toxic copper accumulation in the body, damaging the liver, brain, eyes, and kidneys. Researchers are investigating whether metformin can minimize the condition's effects on mitochondria, which the disease impairs by disrupting the body's ability to remove copper.

stories.title: ATRX gene loss identified as therapeutic target in sarcoma
stories.summary: Researchers at MD Anderson Cancer Center found that sarcomas lacking the ATRX gene are more aggressive than others. The study suggests these tumors may be particularly vulnerable to TEAD inhibitors, identifying the gene loss as both a marker for prognosis and a potential therapeutic target.

stories.title: Health Ministry proposes tighter antimicrobial oversight
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry has proposed bringing all antimicrobials under central regulatory oversight to combat antimicrobial resistance. The move aims to address concerns that state authorities have been granting manufacturing licenses without adequate scrutiny of bioavailability, bioequivalence, or stability studies.

stories.title: Centre proposes changes to drug rules to bring antimicrobials under regulatory oversight
stories.summary: NEW DELHI: The centre has proposed bringing antimicrobials under the central regulatory framework applicable to new drugs to strengthen oversight of their quality, safety and efficacy and address antimicrobial resistance. “The proposed amendment has been initiated in view of concerns regarding the grant of manufacturing licences for antimicrobial products without

stories.title: Health Ministry proposes stricter regulation of antimicrobial drugs to tackle antimicrobial resistance - News On AIR
stories.summary: The Health Ministry has proposed an amendment to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, to include ‘antimicrobials’ in the definition of ‘New Drug’. It has been proposed with a view to strengthening regulatory oversight and addressing the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance AMR. The Ministry said antimicrobial resistance

stories.title: Health Ministry Proposes Amendment to Drug Rules to Bring Antimicrobials Under Central Regulatory Oversight - DD India
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, to bring antimicrobials under the regulatory framework applicable to new drugs, strengthening oversight and addressing the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The proposed amendment, outlined in draft Gazette Notification

stories.title: India integrates wastewater surveillance into health network
stories.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has officially integrated wastewater surveillance into the national health network. The initiative uses sewage samples to detect pathogens and potential pandemic threats before outbreaks occur. National guidelines were released on November 16 to standardize the process across India.

stories.title: CSIR-CCMB Hyderabad helps shape India’s wastewater surveillance guidelines
stories.summary: HYDERABAD: The Union health ministry has released national guidelines to expand wastewater surveillance for detecting infectious diseases, including influenza, monkeypox, hepatitis and cholera, across India. The guidelines aim to help public health authorities identify disease-causing pathogens in wastewater and provide early warnings of potential outbreaks. The ministry released the document

stories.title: India launches syndromic surveillance network across 70 labs
stories.summary: India has launched a syndromic surveillance initiative across 70 laboratories to create an early-warning network for infectious disease outbreaks. Led by the DHR and ICMR, the system uses real-time health data to track four disease syndromes. The initiative was unveiled at a recent health research summit.

stories.title: ICMR creates early-warning network for infectious diseases
stories.summary: The ICMR has launched a syndromic surveillance network across 70 laboratories to monitor infectious disease outbreaks. The system uses real-time health data to track pathogens ranging from common to rare. Priority lists were established following 44 expert meetings to guide the new epidemiological analysis framework.

stories.title: ICMR study finds high vitamin B1 deficiency in Northeast India
stories.summary: A study by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition found that one in five pregnant and lactating women in parts of Assam and Tripura suffer from thiamine deficiency. The research, published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, links the findings to local dietary practices.

stories.title: Thiamine Deficiency Re-Emerges Among Pregnant, Lactating Women In Parts Of Northeast: ICMR-NIN Study - NDTV
Maternal thiamine deficiency flagged in Assam and Tripura
stories.summary: Recent clinical data from the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition reveals significant vitamin B1 shortages among expectant mothers in Assam’s Barak Valley and Tripura. The survey of 1,083 women highlights a recurring public health concern in regions with a history of beriberi. Experts are urging increased antenatal vigilance.

stories.title: Patient group questions TB burden reporting
stories.summary: Jan Swasthya Abhiyan India has challenged official progress reports on tuberculosis, citing the WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026. While the government highlights a 38 percent decline in mortality since 2015, the group notes India still accounts for one-fourth of global cases and 23 percent of deaths.

stories.title: Gaza health ministry: Restrictions on patient evacuations threaten thousands of critical cases - وكالة سبأ
Ebola outbreak in DRC continues to spread at record pace
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remains out of control six months after its declaration. Infections and deaths are rising at double the rate of previous records. Health workers face insecurity and distrust, hampering containment efforts in the region.

stories.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches record scale
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in over 11,000 infections and 5,500 deaths since May. Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, the virus is spreading faster than any previous outbreak on record. Aid efforts are currently hindered by resource shortages and insecurity.

stories.title: United States loses measles elimination status
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organisation has revoked the measles elimination status of the United States after 26 years. The decision follows 5,400 reported cases in 2026, the highest annual total since 1991. Unicef data indicates 96 percent of cases involve unvaccinated individuals or those with unknown status.

stories.title: Measles circulating nonstop in U.S. for over a year
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organisation has revoked the measles elimination status of the United States, citing continuous virus circulation for more than a year. Director Dr. Jarbas Barbosa stated that the loss of status puts communities at risk of a preventable disease, reversing decades of public health progress.

stories.title: EU officials call for action on antimicrobial resistance
stories.summary: European health officials are calling for urgent intervention following new reports on antibiotic consumption and antimicrobial resistance. The data presents a mixed picture regarding the effectiveness of current measures to curb the rise of resistant pathogens across the continent.

stories.title: Inquiry finds UK border failures left country vulnerable to Covid
stories.summary: A report from the Covid-19 inquiry concluded that the lack of international border controls left the UK extremely vulnerable at the start of the pandemic. Chair Heather Hallett noted that failures in test-and-trace systems allowed the virus to spread unchecked, leaving decision-makers blind to the scale.

stories.title: Study questions malaria monoclonal antibody strategy
stories.summary: Researchers testing the monoclonal antibody L9LS in Malian infants found it was 78 percent effective against malaria over a six-month season. The study casts doubt on the strategy of combining the antibody with existing vaccines, as the results were similar to those achieved by vaccines alone.

stories.title: Gilead signs generic deals for experimental Ebola drug
stories.summary: Gilead Sciences has signed royalty-free deals with three generic drugmakers to produce its experimental Ebola drug, obeldesivir, for 127 low-income countries. The drug is currently in late-stage trials and has not yet received regulatory approval for any use in any country.

stories.title: BIMSTEC adopts 2026-2030 health plan
stories.summary: BIMSTEC health ministers have adopted a new plan of action to coordinate disease preparedness across the Bay of Bengal. The framework includes initiatives for antimicrobial resistance, digital health, and telemedicine. Member states also noted India's progress in establishing a regional centre for traditional medicine.

stories.title: Spain's Wilco raises €2.5M for AI that keeps clinic patients from dropping off - Dealroom
August AI raises $12 million for healthcare assistant
stories.summary: AI healthtech startup August AI has raised $12 million from investors including Accel and Peak XV Partners. The company plans to expand its assistant’s ability to book appointments and manage insurance claims. The startup claims to have helped 10 million people understand their health through its platform.

stories.title: IntelliProve raises €2.7M to bring health monitoring from smartphones to humanoid robots - Tech.eu
Ghent-based IntelliProve raises €2.7 million to monitor vital signs with a 30-second face scan using any camera - EU-Sta
IntelliProve raises €2.7M to turn cameras into health sensors
stories.summary: Belgian startup IntelliProve has raised €2.7 million to measure six health biomarkers through a 30-second face scan. The company aims to move its technology from virtual care into humanoid robots. Smartphones and laptops have cameras, and the company intends to use them for health monitoring without wearables.

stories.title: IntelliProve raises €2.7M to put its face-scan health check on robots - Dealroom
Former Swappie CEO’s healthtech startup secures €3 million pre-seed to help patients get the right care in - ArcticStart
Swappie co-founder’s AI HealthTech startup Treat raises €3 million to streamline private healthcare - EU-Startups
Treat raises €3M to connect patients to doctors
stories.summary: Helsinki-based AI healthtech company Treat has raised €3 million in pre-seed funding led by byFounders and Illusian. Founded by former Swappie CEO Sami Marttinen and others, the platform claims to connect patients to doctors in minutes. The deal was reportedly completed in one week.

stories.title: Finnish healthtech Treat raises €3M to tackle inefficiencies in private healthcare - Tech.eu
Data interoperability remains a challenge in critical care
stories.summary: In intensive care units, fragmented data across monitors, ventilators and electronic health records forces clinicians to spend time locating and reconciling information. Integration is described as a clinical priority rather than an IT requirement, as systems currently struggle to exchange the rapidly changing picture of a patient.

stories.title: ICMR hits 100 technology transfer deals
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research has completed 100 technology transfer deals in less than two years under its Medical Innovations Patent Mitra initiative. At a recent summit, 20 licensing agreements were exchanged with nine companies to help bridge the gap between research and commercial health technologies.

stories.title: UK to study impact of social media ban on youth
stories.summary: Researchers will track 300,000 young people to understand how the UK's upcoming social media ban for under-16s affects mental health. Ten projects across England, Wales and Scotland will examine phone habits and alternative activities. The ban is scheduled to begin in spring 2027.

stories.title: UK launches large-scale study on youth social media ban
stories.summary: More than 300,000 young people will participate in a study examining the effects of the UK's planned social media ban for under-16s. Ten research projects will monitor changes in phone habits and daily activities ahead of the government restrictions, which are set to take effect in 2027.

stories.title: UK Social Media Ban for Under-16s Gets Largest Mental Health Study Yet - Around Prague
Study links youth wellbeing to home life over screen time
stories.summary: A study of 15,925 people across 16 countries found that household finances, safety and relationships with caregivers were more strongly associated with wellbeing than online habits. While frequent short-video scrolling was linked to loneliness, the findings suggest factors beyond screen time are central to the debate.

stories.title: Smartphone tool shows promise for eating disorder support
stories.summary: Researchers have determined that a digital tool designed to encourage help-seeking among young people with eating disorders is feasible and acceptable. The findings support the development of a larger clinical trial to test the tool's effectiveness in providing early support.

stories.title: Study finds Reddit peer advice often matches clinical guidance
stories.summary: A Flinders University study of 1,065 Reddit posts found that peer advice in mental health communities often aligns with clinical guidelines. However, the study notes that this support falls short when users are in crisis, highlighting a gap for a school sector already operating beyond capacity.

stories.title: Students increasingly turn to AI for mental health support
stories.summary: The Cibyl Student Mental Health Study 2026 reports that 33 percent of students and recent graduates use AI tools for mental health, with 18 percent naming chatbots as a primary resource. Meanwhile, reliance on human routes like friends, family and medical teams has declined since 2021.

stories.title: Trevor Project reports AI chatbot use among LGBTQ+ youth
stories.summary: A report from The Trevor Project found that four in 10 queer young people have used AI chatbots for mental health support. While many turn to the technology to overcome barriers to care, the research indicates that most users are not comfortable with the tech itself.

stories.title: Children recover faster than adults in migrant mental health study
stories.summary: A retrospective study of 672 displaced individuals in Mexico City found that children show faster clinical recovery than adults after receiving care for torture and ill-treatment. The research aims to address a historical lack of empirical evidence regarding therapeutic outcomes for forcibly displaced survivors in humanitarian settings.

stories.title: SumDU students contribute to youth mental health research in Ukraine
stories.summary: SumDU students Anna Kobyletska and Maksym Yakovenchuk conducted fieldwork for an international study on adolescent mental health in Ukraine. The project, led by Doctors of the World Greece, examines how war-related stress affects youth and identifies barriers that prevent teenagers from seeking necessary mental health support.

stories.title: Study links weekly park visits to improved mental health
stories.summary: University of Exeter researchers found that children who visited a park at least once a week in the 1990s scored 16.5 percent better on mental health assessments. While outdoor time has declined as screen use rose, the data suggests nature remains a factor in childhood well-being.

research.title: Harnessing smartwatches to spot undiagnosed hypertension
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 19 November 2026, doi:10.1038/d41591-026-00058-8 With the help of artificial intelligence, a consumer smartwatch performed similarly to office-based hypertension measurement in a prospective clinical study, which suggests a new strategy for population-level opportunistic screening.

research.title: Multicenter characterization of enterocolitis associated with BCMA-directed CAR T cell therapy
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 19 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04783-y In a large multicenter case series, only 32% of patients who developed immune effector cell-associated enterocolitis following treatment with BCMA-directed CAR T cells had achieved disease resolution at last follow-up, with some deaths directly attributable to complications of this disorder.

research.title: Scientists discover a hidden hereditary form of aggressive prostate cancer
research.summary: Scientists have discovered a rare inherited mutation in the CDK12 gene linked to aggressive prostate cancer, with all five identified carriers developing metastatic disease between ages 44 and 62. The finding could lead to expanded genetic testing, helping families uncover hidden cancer risks and potentially detect the disease.

research.title: Why don't weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy work for everyone?
research.summary: Why do Ozempic and Wegovy produce dramatic weight loss for some people but disappointing results for others? Scientists are investigating whether the body's hidden energy-saving response could help explain the difference and unlock more effective, personalized weight-loss treatments.
